passages.title: Article: a four-day work week
passages.body:
A MIDSIZE FIRM TRIES A FOUR-DAY WEEK

LEEDS (April 11) — When Calder Logistics announced last year that its 140 employees would work four days a week for the same pay, many competitors were skeptical. Twelve months later, the results are difficult to dismiss. Absences fell by a third, and the number of resignations dropped from fourteen to four. Revenue, meanwhile, rose by 6 percent.

Managing director Sophie Lang said the change was not a perk but a strategy. "We were losing good people to larger firms that could pay more," she said. "We could not compete on salary, so we competed on time."

Not everything went smoothly. Customer-service staff initially struggled to cover all five days, and the company hired three part-time workers to fill the gap. Ms. Lang also admitted that some managers found it hard to let go of the habit of measuring effort by hours rather than results.

Several other firms in the region have since asked to visit Calder's offices to learn how the system works. Ms. Lang says she will welcome them, "though I would warn them that it only works if you redesign meetings first."

passages.title: Report: customer satisfaction
passages.body:
HARLOW TELECOM — CUSTOMER SATISFACTION REPORT, Q3 SUMMARY

Overall satisfaction: 78% (Q2: 74%)

By channel:
• Phone support: 71% (Q2: 75%)
• Online chat: 84% (Q2: 70%)
• In-store: 82% (Q2: 80%)

Main sources of complaints (share of all complaints):
• Long waiting times on the phone: 41%
• Billing errors: 27%
• Unclear contracts: 19%
• Other: 13%

Recommendations:
1. Redirect some phone staff to the chat service, which costs less per contact and is rated higher by customers.
2. Review the billing software before the end of Q4.
3. Simplify contract language. A pilot in the Leeds store reduced related complaints by half.

passages.title: Email chain: contract renewal
passages.body:
From: Priya Shah, Meridian Foods
To: Tom Wyatt, Eastway Packaging
Date: September 5
Subject: Re: Contract renewal

Tom, thank you for the revised draft. We are happy with the unit price of $0.42 and with the delivery schedule. However, clause 7 worries us: it allows Eastway to raise prices with only 30 days' notice. Given the volatility of paper costs, we understand the need for flexibility, but we would like the notice period extended to 90 days, and any increase capped at 5 percent a year. If you can agree to this, I am confident we can sign by September 20.

- - - - - - - - - -

From: Tom Wyatt, Eastway Packaging
To: Priya Shah, Meridian Foods
Date: September 6
Subject: Re: Re: Contract renewal

Priya, I appreciate the clarity. A 90-day notice period is acceptable. A fixed cap is harder: our costs have moved by as much as 12 percent in a single year. What I can offer is a cap of 8 percent, with an additional clause allowing you to end the contract without penalty if an increase exceeds 5 percent. I hope this works. I can send an amended draft tomorrow.

passages.title: Job posting and cover letter
passages.body:
NORTHGATE RETAIL — Assistant Procurement Manager

Northgate Retail seeks an Assistant Procurement Manager to support our sourcing team.

Requirements:
• At least three years of experience in procurement or purchasing
• A degree in business or a related field
• Working knowledge of Spanish or Portuguese (many of our suppliers are in Latin America)
• Willingness to travel up to four weeks per year

Preferred: experience with SAP software.

To apply, send a cover letter and two references by March 15.

- - - - - - - - - -

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the position of Assistant Procurement Manager. I hold a degree in economics and have spent four years as a purchasing officer at Brightwell Foods, where I managed relationships with suppliers in Mexico and Colombia. My Spanish is fluent, although I do not speak Portuguese.

I have worked with Oracle rather than SAP, but I learn new systems quickly. I am glad to travel as required, though I would need the schedule in advance because of family commitments. References from my current director and from a supplier are enclosed.

Sincerely,
Daniel Mora
